prompts.cover:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a finished literary short-story cover for The Last Passenger, portrait 9:16, ideally 864x1536. Input image is ONLY a reference for Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil brushwork and organized value shapes, not its orchard subject. Broad varied directional opaque strokes, connected dark shapes, selected impasto and simplified coherent figures/architecture, subdued night palette, no gloss or uniform embossed strokes.
Night over an evacuated city avenue: a seven-storey radio station on the left, a broad lower third-floor furniture-shop roof on the right with a small open stair doorway emitting yellow practical light. Moon partly behind a strip of cloud. Strong vertical sense of the dark gap between roofs. In the lower-middle, Cerys/Skylark, a slim young ADULT woman with short dark brown curls and medium warm-brown skin, hovers precariously carrying one ordinary adult man in a secure cradle carry, one arm behind his shoulders, one under his bent knees. She wears a simple blue long-sleeved superhero costume with a small yellow bird sewn over the breast, blue trousers/boots, NO cape, NO wings, NO pockets. Vane is in a sleeveless grey vest, trousers and heavy boots, short slicked dark hair, wrist restraints together in front of his stomach. Both are small, embodied figures, anatomically coherent, exhausted rather than glamorous. Far above and behind, a more imposing man stands on the radio-station roof: navy superhero suit, red cape, simple abstract white chest insignia, one hand gripping the broken stem of an aerial whose red warning light is failing. He is a looming silhouette, controlled and frightening, not shouting. Use negative sky and rooftops to invite a story about a rescuer confronting her once-trusted hero; not a crowded plot montage. Moon and lit studio windows motivate light. No blood, corpse, graphic injury, fire, lightning or explosions.
Text verbatim, exact title once only as readable dignified cream painted serif lettering in the upper portion: "The Last Passenger". No subtitle, author name, logo or other text. Preserve a generous legible title area.

Paint the evacuated crossing between two roofs at night, after the incident. View obliquely from the broad THIRD-FLOOR furniture-shop rooftop foreground, with dark gravel, a low brick parapet, and a small stairwell doorway open onto a warm-yellow-lit flight of stairs leading DOWN inside to the loading yard. Across a narrow ordinary avenue is a much taller SEVEN-STOREY radio-station building with broken upper-floor studio windows; its roof is visibly above the observer, roughly four floors higher. The radio aerial has been ripped from its mountings; its bent broken lattice lies across the EMPTY avenue far below. Keep the broken roof mounting visually coherent. Both complete buildings can be glimpsed enough to understand the high-to-low crossing; human-scale low rooftops, not skyscrapers or fantasy towers. A distant skyline recedes in quiet connected shadows. Moon partially obscured by a strip of cloud gives muted slate, grey-violet and soft silver notes; studio windows and stair doorway are only motivated small warm accents, not dramatic orange-blue lighting. Coherent brick/window and stair geometry. Composition should make the lit low door feel reachable across a terrifying dark gap. An evocative location painting, not a labeled diagram or a plot montage.
NO characters, no blood, no bodies, no fire, no explosions, no lightning, no wings. No text, labels or title. Preserve night, distinct 7th/3rd floor roof levels, gravel/parapet, warm open stair door, broken radio mast and empty avenue.
